newsitem.title: USA: ATHLETICS-SLANEY SLAMS U.S. TRACK BODY.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-SLANEY SLAMS U.S. TRACK BODY.

text.p: Veteran American runner Mary Slaney is in a rage over what she believes was the misreading and leaking of her drug testing results by the U.S. ruling body for her sport, USA Track & Field.

"I don't feel like giving anything to the sport right now," Slaney said in an interview with the Eugene Register-Guard published Sunday. "If someone were to ask me how I feel about USA Track & Field right now, I would say I hope it burns in hell."
In 25 years of elite racing, Slaney has experienced the highs of winning two world championships and the lows of numerous injuries and her infamous collision with Zola Budd in the 1984 Olympics.
But never has she been as boiling mad as she is now, since a report of her confidential urine test from last June's U.S. Olympic Trials was published by the New York Times.
Her urinalysis was reported to have shown a suspicious ratio of testosterone to epitestosterone, above the 6-to-1 level considered to be evidence of performance-enhancing drugs.
While the testosterone-to-epitestosterone level, or T/E, is considered constant in men, the ratio can vary in women depending on age, menstrual cycle and use of birth control pills.
At the time of her urine test at the U.S. Trials, Slaney, then 37, was menstruating and had recently begun taking birth control pills.
Slaney and her representatives say these factors could have skewed her T/E ratio enough to call into suspicion her urinalysis last June.

"I've made Olympic teams in the past, I've broken world and American records, I've been drug-tested hundreds of times," Slaney told the Register-Guard. "At my age, you don't start taking performance-enhancing substances to see what you can get out of the sport."

Last August the international ruling body, the IAAF, said it did not have enough information to declare Slaney's drug test positive. By February the IAAF told USA Track & Field to proceed with the case against Slaney. USA Track & Field's Custodial Board filed its findings on May 6.
Slaney's attorney, Doriane Lambelet Coleman, has until Tuesday to file a rebuttal to the Custodial Board.

"I was horrified," Slaney said of how she felt when first informed of the test results last July. "My first response was how can I come up with any sort of questionable results in a drug test when I haven't taken anything?"

With her case pending, Slaney said she intends to compete in the USA Track & Field Championships June 11-15 with a goal of qualifying in the 1,500 meters for the U.S. team at the World Championships in Athens. A leg injury forced her to withdraw from Sunday's Prefontaine Classic here.
